Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have earned acclaim from critics, audiences, and award bodies alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman escaping an abusive partner who turns to technology‑based terror. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this gangster caper. The film’s intricate plot twists and sharp dialogue keep viewers guessing. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | Though more of a courtroom drama, its investigative and conspiratorial underpinnings make it a compelling crime‑thriller. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp script and ensemble cast deliver a tense, historically resonant narrative. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish thriller that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse. The film’s moral ambiguity and relentless pacing create a gripping, unsettling experience. |
| 5 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A period crime‑thriller set in 1840s Tasmania. The film’s stark cinematography and intense revenge plot make it a standout in the genre. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑thriller that examines truth, justice, and gender dynamics. Scott’s meticulous production design and the film’s moral complexity elevate it above typical period pieces. |
| 7 | **The Invisible Man** (2020) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman escaping an abusive partner who turns to technology‑based terror. |

| 9 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | Though more of a courtroom drama, its investigative and conspiratorial underpinnings make it a compelling crime‑thriller. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp script and ensemble cast deliver a tense, historically resonant narrative. |
|10 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish thriller that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse. The film’s moral ambiguity and relentless pacing create a gripping, unsettling experience. |

### How to Choose

- **If you like slick, stylized action**: *The Gentlemen* or *The Invisible Man*.
- **If you prefer a grounded, character‑driven story**: *The Hunt* or *The Nightingale*.
- **If you’re into historical or courtroom drama with thriller elements**: *The Trial of the Chicago 7* or *The Last Duel*.

All of these films were released in 2020 (either in theaters, on streaming platforms, or both) and have received strong reviews from major outlets such as *The New York Times*, *Variety*, and *Rotten Tomatoes*. Happy watching!
